name: ON.energy
headquarters: Miami, Florida, United States (offices: Houston, San Francisco, Mexico, Peru)
ownership: private — >$250M cumulative capital (equity + project debt, company figure as of Dec 2024): $20M Series B led by Ultra Capital with Phalanx Impact Partners (Jun 2023); $25M debt from Lombard Odier (Apr 2024); $40M Palo Verde project financing (Dec 2023); $77.6M Palo de Agua construction credit from Pathward NA + BridgePeak (Jan 2025). No Series C or valuation disclosed; how the 5 GW Crusoe buildout is financed is undisclosed — the key open question.
summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: ON.energy has executed the purest AIDC pivot in the storage sector — from a LatAm-origin merchant BESS developer/integrator (~240 MWh verified in ERCOT; CATL-supplied legacy fleet across Peru, Mexico, Chile, Colombia, Honduras) into a 'grid-safe AI data-center power' vendor built around AI UPS™: a patented medium-voltage, BESS-based uninterruptible power system that sits inline between grid and AI campus, buffering GPU load transients (30→100% swings in 10ms-1s) and riding through voltage faults. Launched October 2025, patented May 2026, zero-voltage ride-through demonstrated in independent testing May 2026, first unit commissioned at the National Laboratory of the Rockies (Flatirons, 13.2 kV) in January 2026 — and then the anchor: a 5 GW AI UPS deployment agreement with Crusoe across multiple hyperscale campuses, commissioning 2026-2027 (July 2026). The supporting supply chain is being deliberately assembled FEOC-clean and US-made — EPC Power grid-forming PCS (Nov 2025), Prolec GE 5 GW of pad-mount transformers (Dec 2025), Shoals eBOS (Feb 2026) — with the battery-cell supplier for AI UPS conspicuously unnamed. This is a direct product-category competitor to Hithium's own December 2025 ∞Power AI-data-center push (1300Ah cell, 6.9 MW/55.2 MWh system): assume Hithium is designed out of the US product, while the dormant LatAm franchise remains a non-FEOC channel where Hithium could plausibly supply.
ecosystemRole: We assess ON.energy as the inverse of the gas-bridge cohort: instead of displacing BESS with generation, it is productizing BESS itself into the AIDC power chain — as a medium-voltage UPS category that competes with Vertiv/Eaton/Schneider conventional UPS on one flank and with Hithium's AI-data-center product line on the other. The 5 GW Crusoe award makes it arguably the most visible BESS-based power-buffer vendor in ERCOT, validated against NOGRR 282 large-load ride-through requirements. Its choices now shape the category's supply-chain norms: a FEOC-clean, US-made stack with an unnamed cell supplier is the template Hithium's US competitors will replicate — and the single most valuable intelligence question is who wins that cell contract.

productsAndServices.name: AI UPS™ (the pivot product)
productsAndServices.description: A patented medium-voltage, BESS-based UPS purpose-built for AI data centers — 'the world's first MV UPS' (company claim at the Oct 22, 2025 launch). Sits inline between the grid and the AI campus at medium voltage (demonstrated at 13.2 kV), buffering GPU load transients (30→100% swings in 10ms-1s windows) in both directions — protecting the campus from grid faults (zero-voltage ride-through demonstrated in independent testing, May 2026) and protecting the grid from the campus's load swings (the ERCOT NOGRR 282 / Large Load Interconnection compliance problem). MV UPS patent awarded May 2026. First unit built and commissioned at the National Laboratory of the Rockies' Flatirons Campus (ARIES controllable-grid-interface testing; contract-to-construction under 6 months). Revenue model: technology provider plus owner-operator, with a claimed market-participation kicker of 'millions per year per 100 MW of IT load.'
productsAndServices.positioning: Creates a new category between conventional low-voltage UPS (Vertiv, Eaton, Schneider) and grid-scale BESS — and lands directly on Hithium's own ∞Power AI-data-center product territory (Dec 2025: 1300Ah cell, 6.9 MW/55.2 MWh system, grid-buffering positioning). Moat claims: MV-level rather than LV, NOGRR 282/LLVRT compliance, ERCOT LLI validation, FEOC-compliant US-built supply chain.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct partnership agreements with data-center developers/operators (Crusoe anchor); technology-provider-plus-owner-operator structures
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Hyperscale AI campuses in ERCOT and other large-load jurisdictions facing ride-through mandates and interconnection friction
productsAndServices.roadmap: 5 GW Crusoe deployment commissioning 2026-2027 across multiple hyperscale campuses; watch the unnamed cell award, the financing structure, and whether ERCOT's NOGRR 282 enforcement drives copycat procurement.

productsAndServices.name: FEOC-clean component stack (assembled 2025-2026)
productsAndServices.description: Deliberately US-sourced supply chain for AI UPS: EPC Power grid-forming PCS partnership (Nov 2025); Prolec GE — 'the largest dedicated transformer deal in the US,' 5 GW of pad-mount transformers (Dec 2025); Shoals Technologies DC recombiners/eBOS, multi-GW, for a 'leading AI data-center operator' (Feb 2026 — Crusoe inferred). Battery cells for AI UPS are unnamed; the website claims 'FEOC-compliant, engineered and built in America.' Company claims '10+ GW production capacity ready' (marketing figure). Proprietary On.Command™ EMS (10+ years of development) is the integration layer; Always.On MV industrial UPS was the precursor product.
productsAndServices.positioning: The procurement architecture is the message: post-OBBBA, a BESS-based product aimed at US hyperscale campuses is being built with zero Chinese content by design — despite the company's own legacy fleet being CATL-supplied, which signals pragmatic rather than ideological sourcing.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Component supply agreements feeding the Crusoe deployment
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Internal supply for AI UPS deployments
productsAndServices.roadmap: The cell contract is the open slot — a US-manufactured LFP supplier (or a §45X-qualified transplant) is the natural fit; any award will be a category-defining precedent.

productsAndServices.name: Legacy merchant BESS & LatAm integration franchise
productsAndServices.description: ERCOT: ~80 MWh Palo Verde portfolio operating (COD ~Q3 2024; $40M financing Dec 2023) plus 160 MWh Palo de Agua ($77.6M construction credit, Jan 2025) — ~240 MWh verified. Dec 2024 snapshot: 320 MWh operating/under construction including LatAm, >1.5 GWh pipeline, ~80% equity retained in its own projects. LatAm first-mover history: distributed BESS across Peru, Mexico, Chile, Colombia, Honduras on the On.Command EMS — genuinely early, now publicly dormant since the pivot (no LatAm project news in the trailing 18 months). Current company claims of '3+ GW operating/under construction (storage + UPS)' and '75+ projects' almost certainly count contracted AI UPS bookings, not commissioned assets.
productsAndServices.positioning: As an ERCOT merchant BESS owner it is immaterial (~240 MWh vs multi-GWh at Jupiter/Plus Power/Eolian). The LatAm franchise is the strategically interesting remainder: a non-FEOC market where the company has installed base, relationships, and an EMS — and where its historic CATL sourcing shows Chinese cells are acceptable.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Project development with retained equity; historic integration contracts
productsAndServices.targetSegments: ERCOT merchant (legacy); LatAm C&I and grid (dormant)
productsAndServices.roadmap: Whether the LatAm arm revives — and with whose cells — is the Hithium-relevant watch item.

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess ON.energy as a direct product-category competitor to Hithium in AIDC — not a prospective customer in the US. Its AI UPS occupies the same grid-buffering, transient-absorbing socket as Hithium's December 2025 ∞Power AI-data-center system, and its supply chain is being assembled explicitly FEOC-clean while Hithium carries the NDAA §154 designation. Assume designed-out of the US product line.

(High confidence) The unnamed AI UPS cell supplier is the single most valuable open question this dossier tracks: a 5 GW deployment implies one of the largest non-Chinese cell procurements in the US market, and whoever wins it (US-made LFP, a §45X-qualified transplant, or a Korean incumbent) sets the precedent for the whole BESS-as-UPS category's sourcing norms.

(Medium confidence) The Crusoe deal's financing is unproven scaffolding: >$250M lifetime capital against a 5 GW buildout implies project-level structures or a major raise that has not surfaced. Slippage risk is real — the company's own '3+ GW / 10+ GW' claims already run far ahead of ~240 MWh of verified operating assets, and a delayed or shrunk Crusoe program would deflate the category's first-mover claim.

(Medium confidence) The dormant LatAm franchise is the one plausible Hithium opening: Peru/Mexico/Chile installed base, a proprietary EMS, no FEOC constraint, and a demonstrated history of buying Chinese cells (CATL). If the AI UPS business succeeds, a revived LatAm arm would need cost-competitive cells outside the US policy perimeter — a fit for Hithium's non-US channel strategy worth a standing watch.

(Low confidence) Conventional UPS incumbents (Vertiv, Eaton, Schneider) and large BESS OEMs will contest the MV-UPS category within 12-24 months; ON.energy's patent and NOGRR 282 validation are early moats, but the company's thin balance sheet against incumbents' scale makes acquisition a plausible endgame — which would instantly re-rate the category.
